r.t: Endur Scaling is a branch of Proven Ability Scaling. However, there are a substantial amount of key differences between the two scalings, which warranted the creation of this one. This document will hopefully explain to the fullest the complete rules of how the scaling works and how to use it properly.

PA (Proven Ability) Scaling moves from the proven to the provable when evaluating feats, it operates under the idea of Empirical Evidence and Logical Proof, which is contradictory to Stop’s scaling for example, which only emphasises Empirical Evidence and dismisses all logical evidence.

‘I’ll disclose shortly how to evaluate PA depending on the type of feat/statement presented, but first, I should elaborate on the fact that while scaling PA allows and heavily encourages interpretation and analysis, it does NOT support baseless assumptions like in Assumed Ability Scaling, known as Narrative or Normal Scaling otherwise; characters can never be scaled beyond what can be proven they can perform.

Any given character can be comfortably scaled to where their feats are, and more so, they can be scaled slightly higher in certain categories if it’s provable without assumptions or vague interpretations that such scaling would be logically possible.

On-screen and off-screen feats hold the same degree of importance, though it’s obviously easier to argue with on-screen feats, the only measurement of superiority between them is the quality of the feat itself’
This is an insert from Cento’s document on

. Endur’s Scaling works the same way with the only difference being, it puts less of an emphasis on the ‘Narrative’ of characters.

This means that someone's ability won't be scaled from their implied narrative of being equal to another character unless they have the feats to back it up.

Endur Scaling is limited to only determining the winner in a ‘General Outsmarting Situation’. The reason is that the importance placed on specific categories relies on the situation staying constant. If you change the situation, then new categories will take more importance, which would then nullify the use of this scaling.

Now to explain what this ‘General Outsmarting Situation’ actually is.

Unlike a non-fixed situation, there are rules. The rules are not as strict as a fixed situation allowing room for categories such as manipulation however they’re valued less than in non-fixed. This outsmarting scenario tests the general ability of a character by mixing the themes of FS + NFS.

Something quite exclusive to this scaling is the ‘Equalised Cosmology’ of the environment these characters will be scaled in. To put it simply, they will be put into a separate Universe with logic akin to our own world. This means feats must follow a sense of Logic and Reason to be applicable in this ‘Equalised Cosmology’. For Example, a strategy used by a character may have many layers to it, which in normal scaling, would attribute to that character’s Strategy Complexity. However, in this scaling, if the layers themselves do not make sense or are not applicable in the world this scaling puts them in, then the feat will not be recognised at all. Any feats that are clearly controlled by narrative or plot convenience will not be seen as legitimate in this scaling.

Here the doc will list all of the categories that will be used in this type of scaling. They will be divided up into sections to minimise confusion. Each main category will have the factors that make it up below, next to the ‘=’. At the end of each section, there will be a few notes describing how these categories will be scaled along with any additional remarks. The number in blue out of 100 represents its general importance in a GOS.
= Logical Reasoning + Learning Ability + Adaptability + CPI + NCPS + Abstract Reasoning
= Overall Knowledge + Ability to recall/apply knowledge
= Emotional Management + Emotional Engagement + Emotional Perception + Emotional Understanding
The factors shown above will determine the distribution of categories in the Emotional Intelligence section. All factors will hold equal correlation to their respective category.
= Direct Manipulation + Indirect Manipulation + Logical Manipulation + Emotional Manipulation
= Acting Skills + Misdirection + S. Deception + V. Deception + Info Control
The most practical form of Deception in this scaling is Acting Skills due to the fact you don't need any external factors. Misdirection is a more effective form of Deception.
= Strategy Complexity + Strategy Success Rate + Strategy Adaptability + Strategy Control
= Planning Coverage + Planning Preparation + Greater Limitations

= Actual Anticipation + Logical Prediction + Setting Traps + Trap Evasion

Actual Anticipation is a very rare category that will only be given to characters who display a proper ability to perfectly anticipate something, using a deductive process, or sometimes an Inductive Process.

Logical Reasoning will not be treated as an ‘Overall Category’ in this section, but rather it will be awarded to the character who makes more sound and valid inferences in their reasoning. This means that a character can take 1 out of the 3 categories, but still take Logical Reasoning.
= Short Term Memory + Long Term Memory + Working Memory

In total there is a maximum of 47 categories that can be used to judge who outsmarts in a GOS in Endur Scaling. There may be times where Memory and Adaptability have to be split into their respective sub-categories.

. I decided to make this type of scaling as I heavily agreed with the way Proven Ability Scaling worked but I wanted to limit the number of categories being used. I also wanted to introduce the idea of placing more importance on specific categories than others, as many scaled by the number of categories a character got, instead of the value of categories that character got.
 I hope people can come to respect this scaling along with Proven Ability Scaling and recognise it as being legitimate.
